summary: The way an LDP speaker advertises labels for a Forwarding Equivalence Class depends on the FEC type, not necessarily on the session's negotiated mode. This document updates RFC 5036 to say so and specifies the advertisement mode for all FEC types defined at the time.

eli5.summary: Routers hand out numbered tags to mark traffic. This RFC clears up that the type of traffic decides how tags are offered, whatever the routers first agreed to.

subtitle: Clarifies that the kind of FEC, not just the session's negotiated mode, decides how an LDP speaker advertises labels.

tldr.problem: LDP lets two routers negotiate one label advertisement mode per session, but for some FEC types the advertising behavior is set by the FEC type, and the specifications did not say which was which.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7358 updates RFC 5036 to say the negotiated mode is only indicative, requires every document defining an LDP FEC to state its advertisement discipline, and fills in the discipline for every FEC type defined at the time, also adding a column to the IANA registry.
tldr.outcome: Each FEC type now has a stated discipline (DU, DoD, as negotiated, upstream, not applicable or unknown), which removes ambiguity when several FEC types share one LDP session.

facts.label: Discipline values
facts.value: 6: DU, DoD, As negotiated, Upstream, Not applicable, Unknown

today: RFC 7358 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is the document that updates RFC 3212, RFC 4447, RFC 5036, RFC 5918, RFC 6388 and RFC 7140 on this point.

sections.title: Why the Mode Is Only a Hint
sections.content:
The Label Distribution Protocol (LDP, RFC 5036) lets two Label Switching Routers (LSRs) negotiate a label advertisement mode when a session starts. Only a single mode is negotiated, agreed upon and used for a given session, and it is carried in the LDP Initialization message.

RFC 7358 points out that this negotiated mode is only indicative. It says how the speakers will advertise labels for some Forwarding Equivalence Classes (FECs), but it is not a rule that restricts them to a specific behavior. For some FEC types, the advertising behavior is governed by the FEC type and not by the negotiated behavior.

The document makes that fact clear by updating RFC 5036. It also updates RFC 3212, RFC 4447, RFC 5918, RFC 6388 and RFC 7140 to say, for each FEC type they define, whether label binding advertisements are constrained by the negotiated mode.
sections.eli5: When two routers meet, they agree on a general way to share numbered tags. But for some kinds of traffic the kind itself already says how tags must be shared, so the first agreement is just a hint.

sections.title: The Six Discipline Types
sections.content:
Several FEC types can share one LDP session. To remove ambiguity and conflict among them, the RFC defines a label advertisement discipline for each FEC type. It introduces six values for that discipline:

  • DU (Downstream Unsolicited)
  • DoD (Downstream on Demand)
  • As negotiated (DU or DoD)
  • Upstream, which refers to RFC 6389
  • Not applicable
  • Unknown

The text does not add new advertisement behavior. It only names the discipline that already applies to each FEC type.
sections.eli5: It makes a short list of labels, like sticky notes, that say how each kind of traffic gets its tags: by one method, by another, by whatever the routers agreed, or not at all.

sections.title: The Update to RFC 5036
sections.content:
Section 3.5.3 of RFC 5036, under the description of the label advertisement discipline, gains two statements. First, each document that defines an LDP FEC must state whether the negotiated label advertisement discipline applies to label binding advertisements for that FEC. If it does not apply, the document must also explicitly state the discipline to be used for the FEC.

Second, RFC 7358 itself defines the discipline for two FEC types from RFC 5036: the Wildcard FEC (type 0x01) is Not applicable, and the Prefix FEC (type 0x02) is As negotiated (DU or DoD).

Section 2.2 adds that the disciplines for the other currently defined FEC types are listed in the IANA section, and that the document updates the respective RFCs in which those FECs were introduced.
sections.eli5: From now on, whoever invents a new kind of traffic has to say how its tags are shared. The RFC also fills in the answer for the two oldest kinds.

sections.title: The Updated IANA Registry
sections.content:
The IANA registry called "Forwarding Equivalence Class (FEC) Type Name Space", under the "Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) Parameters" registry, was extended. A new column titled "Label Advertisement Discipline" was added, taking the six values above. RFC 7358 was made an additional reference for the registry and for all affected registrations, and the other columns were kept as they were.

The resulting table covers the assigned FEC types. Most are DU: P2MP, MP2MP-up, MP2MP-down, HSMP-upstream, PWid, Generalized PWid, Protection and P2MP PW Downstream. CR-LSP is DoD. HSMP-downstream is listed as DU, Upstream, and P2MP PW Upstream as Upstream. Only the Prefix FEC is As negotiated, while Wildcard and Typed Wildcard are Not applicable.
sections.eli5: The official list of traffic kinds got one new column that says how each kind hands out tags.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC only clarifies when an LDP session's label advertisement mode applies. It therefore adds no LDP security mechanics and no new considerations beyond those already defined in the LDP specification, RFC 5036.
sections.eli5: Nothing new is being sent or locked, only explained, so no new safety rules are needed.
